prng.reference: Steele, Lea, Flood, 'Fast Splittable Pseudorandom Number Generators', OOPSLA 2014; constants as in Vigna's splitmix64.c (https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c)
prng.mix64: z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9; z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EB; return z ^ (z >> 31); all arithmetic mod 2^64
prng.draw: draw(seed, i) = mix64(seed + (i + 1) * gamma). This is output i (0-based) of SplitMix64 started at state = seed, so draws are random access and generation can be split across workers.
prng.draw_index: i = ordinal * 16 + sub, sub in 0..15. sub 0 = empty/null/missing decision, sub 1 = value or length, sub 2 = secondary value, sub 3..10 = array elements.
prng.uniform: uniform(u, n) = floor(u * n / 2^64) using a 128-bit product. No rejection; bias below n / 2^64 is accepted and identical in every implementation.
prng.permille: a draw u passes a p-permille test when uniform(u, 1000) < p
prng.stream_seed: stream_seed(name) = mix64(master_seed XOR fnv1a64(utf8(name))); FNV-1a 64-bit, offset 0xCBF29CE484222325, prime 0x100000001B3

affine_selection.rule: For a domain of size N, v(i) = (a * i + b) mod N with gcd(a, N) = 1 is a bijection on [0, N). 'Select exactly K' means select i when v(i) < K. a is the first integer >= floor(N * 0.6180339887498949) coprime to N; b = uniform(draw(stream_seed(stream), 0), N).
affine_selection.why: Exact counts with closed-form indexing. Residue classes of i (site, slot) are spread evenly over [0, N), so no selector shares a modulus with the site rule.

uuid.ordinal_format: decimal ASCII, no padding, no sign

site_rule: site = the site whose group_residues_mod_40 contains (global group ordinal mod 40)

retained_fixture.group_ordinal: g = month_index * 1000000 + m, m = month-local ordinal 0..999999
retained_fixture.local_calendar: Month and day are site-local calendar dates in the site timezone. Exactly 10,000,000 events per site-local calendar month; UTC-month totals differ slightly and are published by the generator.
retained_fixture.day_placement: v = day_placement affine value of m. With D days in the month, local day d (0-based) holds the groups with ceil(d * 1000000 / D) <= v < ceil((d + 1) * 1000000 / D).

start_time.rule: t0 = lo + uniform(draw(group.start_time, g * 16 + 1), hi - lo + 1) seconds
start_time.hi: min(instant of local 23:50:00 on that date, fixture_end_exclusive - 300 s)
start_time.dst: Instants come from IANA rules, so the interval is 23 h or 25 h long on transition days.
start_time.event_times: slot s at t0 + 30 * s seconds; the last event is at most 23:54:30 local, so no group crosses local midnight

client_inputs.ip: IPv6 2001:db8::/32 documentation prefix; address = 2001:db8:0:0:0:0:{g >> 16 & 0xffff:x}:{g & 0xffff:x} in canonical text
client_inputs.why: Generator emits identity inputs, not pseudonyms. The loader and live injection derive pseudonyms with the production derivation from 0001, so late events reach the same identity.

identity.identify_message: Identified groups send identify at t0 - 1 s with id, consent "persistent", and the two session properties. Every event of the group carries the same id. Identify messages are associated records (4,000,000), not primary events.

dimension_rules.coverage: For a dimension with population P and cardinality N, stride = floor(P / N). Record j (dimension ordinal) is a coverage row when j mod stride == 0 and j div stride < N; it takes catalog index j div stride, overriding empty and head draws.
dimension_rules.draw_order: sub 0: empty when the empty_permille test passes. sub 1: head (catalog index 0) when the head_permille test passes. sub 2: zipf rank.
dimension_rules.zipf: Integer weights w_k = floor(2^40 / (k + 1)) for k in 0..N-1, exponent 1. x = uniform(u, sum w); rank = least k with cumulative weight > x. Catalog index = rank.
dimension_rules.list: x = uniform(u, sum weights); value = first catalog entry whose cumulative weight > x
dimension_rules.dimension_ordinal: capture_group dims use g; pageview dims use the pageview ordinal; event_name uses the non-revenue index
dimension_rules.precedence: revenue forcing, then coverage rows, then acceptance plants, then draws
dimension_rules.independence: Group-level and event-level draws are independent apart from the acceptance plants and the performance device multiplier. Observed joint distributions for device, event name, plan, country, and referrer are published by the generator: fixed by milestone 02: fixtures/workload/generated/inventory.json (joint_distributions)

referrer_domain.scope: session field (0004 Field scope); generated per capture group, so every event of a group shares it

path.title: equals the path
path.performance_event_path: path of the pageview in slot 8 of the same group

event_name.revenue_events: always "purchase" (the 32nd name); purchase never comes from this draw
event_name.index: v - 1200000 where v is the revenue affine value of the custom event

acceptance_plants.purpose: Q03 needs mobile signup events with plan=pro on site A and site D in both comparison periods
acceptance_plants.rule: In each local day bucket, groups with v - day_start < 40 are planted. These 40 consecutive v values cover all 40 site residues, so every site gets at least one planted group per day.
acceptance_plants.planted_group: device = mobile; the group's first custom event that is neither a revenue event nor an event_name coverage row becomes event_name signup with slot-0 property plan = pro. If no custom event qualifies, or the device row is a coverage row, the group is not planted.
acceptance_plants.verification: Generation fails if a Q03 case's current or previous period has zero matching events for its site.

event_properties.selection: every custom event (24,000,000) plus 56,000,000 pageviews selected by the pageview_properties affine rule; performance events never carry properties
event_properties.slots: Each selected record has one key per slot: slot 0 string, slot 1 numeric, slot 2 date/bool/array. Key = list draw over the slot's draw_weight (stream prop.slot{n}_key, ordinal e).
event_properties.revenue_events: slot 0 = currency, slot 1 = revenue, slot 2 drawn
event_properties.value_draw: stream prop.value, ordinal e * 3 + slot; sub 0 = null test (null_permille, stored as the null type), sub 1 = value, sub 2 = array length, sub 3..10 = elements
event_properties.missing: A key is missing on every record whose slot drew another key, and on all records without properties. Per-key missing frequency is published: fixed by milestone 02: fixtures/workload/generated/inventory.json (property_keys)

keys.notes: Revenue events only; value follows the revenue rule, never drawn.

values.notes: suffix = ["", " für", " 日本", " 😀"]; non-ASCII on purpose; empty string is a value, not missing
byte length = len("note {i} ") + 6 * (15 + i mod 60); stays under the 500-character limit
Revenue events only. JSON number = minor units / 10^exponent. EUR/USD/GBP tiers have fractions and store as decimal; JPY stores as integer. One key, two types on purpose.
above 2^53 - 1, so responses encode values as decimal strings (0004)

revenue.rule: r = revenue index; currency = [EUR, USD, GBP, JPY][r mod 4]; q = r div 4; tier = q mod 10; amount = tiers_minor[tier]; refund (amount negated) when q mod 500 >= 490
revenue.payload: data.revenue = amount / 10^exponent as a JSON number; data.currency = code
revenue.closed_form: Per currency: 30,000 records per tier, 600 refunds per tier. gross = 29,400 * sum(tiers), refunds = -600 * sum(tiers), net = 28,800 * sum(tiers), count = 300,000.
revenue.rounding: Engines compare integer minor units. Decimal rendering divides by 10^exponent exactly, no rounding. No conversion between currencies.

performance.rule: per metric: sub 0 missing test, then sub 1 zero test (zero_permille), else x = uniform(sub 2, 1000000) and value = linear interpolation between knots with integer floor division, then floor(value * device_multiplier / 1000)
performance.stream: perf.value, ordinal = performance ordinal * 5 + metric index (lcp, fcp, ttfb, inp, cls)
performance.cls_limit: cls max 100 (upstream); the largest generated value is 4.2000

replay.window: the last 14 site-local days of September 2026 (day index 16..29)
replay.selection: candidates are month 11 groups with v >= ceil(16 * 1000000 / 30); i = v - that start; recorded when (a * i + b) mod n < 50000, with n = candidate count and a, b from stream replay.select by the affine rule
replay.timing: fragment j (0..4) at t0 + 60 * j + 1 s; index j, total 5, final marker on j = 4
replay.content: ASCII rrweb JSON from a fixed DOM template set, sliced into 65,536-byte values. Template set: four masked rrweb event templates in crates/workload/src/associated.rs; gzip ratio 11.75, 5,576 compressed bytes per 65,536-byte fragment (fixed by milestone 02). Not random padding.

heatmap.rule: interaction i: day = i div 100000; group = the r-th group of that local day bucket, r = uniform(sub 1, bucket size), so group m = a^-1 * (day_start + r - b) mod 1000000; pageview = uniform(sub 2, pageviews in group)
heatmap.type: click when the 800-permille test passes (sub 0), else scroll
heatmap.click: x = uniform(sub 3, viewportW), pageY = uniform(sub 4, 3000), y = pageY mod viewportH
heatmap.aggregate_cell_key: provisional until milestone 09: (site, path, viewportW, type, x div 32, pageY div 32) for clicks; (site, path, viewportW, scrollPct div 10) for scrolls; one row per UTC day
heatmap.aggregate_rows: to be fixed after first generation by milestone 02

associated_data.labels: Report primary events, property values, session property values, identify messages, replay fragments, heatmap interactions, and aggregate rows as separate counts. The deployment is not a 120M-row dataset.

control_state.users: user A and user B, both authorized for all 12 sites

retention_advance.cutoff: 0006 Retention cutoff. today = local date of the application clock in the site's current timezone. Events: event_time < start of local date today - 12 calendar months. Site A at new_clock removes events before 2025-10-31T23:00:00Z (local date < 2025-11-01); site B (local date 2026-10-31) removes local dates < 2025-10-31.
retention_advance.replay: add 50,000 captures for the last 14 local days of October 2026 by the replay rule; a capture is removed whole when its first fragment is before the start of today - 14 days (0006)

selectivity_classes.selective: matched records <= 0.1% of the case's in-range population
selectivity_classes.rule: Generator checks each labeled case after first generation. A case outside its class gets a different literal before hashes are fixed; the data is never changed for it.

measurement.matched_counts: Each case's matched-record count, expected row count, and golden-result hash are fixed after first generation and never regenerated. A changed hash is a failure, not an update.
measurement.retention_in_queries: Queries apply the 0006 cutoffs as a predicate. Golden results assume the application clock's local date is 2026-10-01 in the queried site's timezone (site A before 2026-10-01T22:00:00Z, site D before 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z). Runs that pass a site's local midnight, such as the 24-hour soak, compare against oracle results for the clock's current local date, which the oracle computes per day.
